candidate.prompt_text: Talk about two places in your town that students often visit. Say what each place is and what people do there.
suggested_ideas: a park, library, market, school gate area, or sports center
simple activities such as walking, reading, buying snacks, meeting friends
clear stress in place words and activity words

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker names two common places in their town and briefly says what people usually do in each place.
evaluation_guide.key_points: Two places are clearly identified; each place has one simple description or activity; speech includes words with noticeable stress such as MA-rket, LI-brary, PLAY-ground, a-ROUND, be-HIND if used.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any neutral, everyday places in a town are acceptable, including a park, market, library, street, lake, school area, bus stop, or sports center. The response may be very simple if understandable.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about one place; describing a place in another country; giving opinions about national politics; discussing a family trip instead of places in town.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Focus on whether word stress in common two- or three-syllable words is produced clearly enough to support understanding. Minor grammar errors are acceptable if pronunciation is the main strength.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Flat stress on all syllables; incorrect stress in common words like li-BRA-ry instead of LI-brary; listing places without saying anything about them; speaking too quietly to judge stress clearly.

candidate.prompt_text: Describe a street or area in your town that you know well. Mention three things people can see there.
suggested_ideas: shops, trees, a small park, a market, a bus stop, or a school
adjectives like busy, quiet, crowded, or clean
careful stress in words with two syllables

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker describes one familiar street or area and names three visible things there.
evaluation_guide.key_points: One street or area is introduced; three things are mentioned; the description is short and concrete; common content words have clear stress.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any familiar area in town is acceptable, such as the road near school, the town center, a small neighborhood street, or the area near a lake or market. The student may use basic vocabulary.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking about a dream city; explaining traffic laws in detail; describing a foreign tourist site; discussing mobile apps or online maps instead of the place itself.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Listen for intelligible stress in words like HO-tel, MAR-ket, TA-ble, GAR-den, QUI-et, CROW-ded. Reward clear emphasis patterns even if the answer is short.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Misplacing stress in familiar words; rushing through a list so stress cannot be heard; giving fewer than three things; focusing only on personal feelings with no description of the area.

candidate.prompt_text: Choose one public place in your town, such as a park or library. Describe it and say why it is useful for students.
suggested_ideas: words like library, study, open, helpful, or peaceful

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker chooses one public place, gives a simple description, and explains one or two ways it helps students.
evaluation_guide.key_points: One public place is named; the place is described briefly; usefulness for students is explained; stress in key words is clear enough for easy understanding.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any neutral public place is acceptable, including a park, library, bookshop, community center, museum, or sports area, as long as the answer stays simple and relevant to students.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking about family members who work there; discussing religion or political events at the place; giving a long history lesson; describing expensive travel to reach the place.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Primary scoring should center on word stress in common words and short phrases, for example LI-brary, MU-seum, HELP-ful, PEACE-ful, STU-dent. Content only needs to be basic and relevant.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Incorrect stress on multi-syllable words; repeating the place name without description; unclear explanation of usefulness; overusing single-word answers that do not provide enough speech to judge pronunciation.
